# Paraguay Territorial Tax System
## The complete guide for European investors and business owners

---

**Version:** 2.0 — April 2026  
**Language:** English  
**For:** Investors and business owners from Netherlands, Germany, Spain

---

:::{.callout-tip}
**Summary:** Paraguay operates under a unique **territorial tax system** — you only pay tax on income generated within the country. Foreign-sourced income pays **0% tax**.
:::

---

## 1. The Territorial System Explained

### The Basic Principle

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           PARAGUAY TERRITORIAL TAX SYSTEM                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                             │
│   PARAGUAY-SOURCED INCOME ────► 10% max (IRE/IRP)          │
│                                                             │
│   FOREIGN-SOURCED INCOME ─────► 0% (not taxed)              │
│                                                             │
│   This rule applies to:                                    │
│   • Dividends from foreign companies                       │
│   • Remote work salary                                    │
│   • Consulting to international clients                  │
│   • Investment returns                                   │
│   • Capital gains                                        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Comparison: Territorial vs Worldwide

| Aspect | Paraguay (Territorial) | Netherlands (Worldwide) | Germany (Worldwide) | Spain (Worldwide) |
|:-------|:---------------------:|:-----------------------:|:------------------:|:----------------:|
| Income in Paraguay | 10% | Taxed | Taxed | Taxed |
| Foreign income | **0%** | Taxed (25-49%) | Taxed (25-45%) | Taxed (19-47%) |
| Foreign dividends | **0%** | 15% | 25% + Soli | 19-26% |
| Capital gains | 0% foreign | 26-31% | 26% | 19-26% |

---

## 2. Tax Rates 2026

### Personal Income Tax (IRP)

| Annual Income (PYG) | Income (USD) | Rate |
|:-------------------|:-------------|:---:|
| 0 - 50,000,000 | $0 - 6,350 | **8%** |
| 50,000,001 - 150,000,000 | $6,350 - 19,000 | **9%** |
| Over 150,000,000 | Over $19,000 | **10%** |

### Corporate Income Tax (IRE)

| Entity Type | Rate | Base |
|:------------|:---:|:----|
| General (SA, SRL, EAS) | **10%** | Net profit |
| SIMPLE Regime | 10% (on 30% gross) | 3% effective |
| Non-profit organizations | 0% | Varies |

### Other Taxes

| Tax | Rate | Trigger |
|:---|:---:|:--------|
| IVA (VAT) | 10% | Sales/services |
| IDU (dividends) | 8% residents | Distribution |
| IDU (dividends) | 15% non-residents | Distribution |
| INR (non-residents) | 4.5-15% | PY-source income |

## 3. Practical Examples

### Example 1: Freelancer with Dutch client (remote)

```
Situation:
├── Income: €5,000/month consulting to NL client
└── Services performed from Paraguay (remote)

Result in Paraguay:
├── Tax: €0 (foreign source)
└── Available: €60,000/year

Comparison:
├── In Netherlands: ~€17,500 tax
├── In Paraguay: €0
└── Savings: €17,500/year
```

### Example 2: Salary from Paraguayan company

```
Situation:
├── Salary: ₲50,000,000/year (~$6,350)
├── Paraguayan company
└── Work performed in Paraguay

Result in Paraguay:
├── IRP: 8% on ₲50,000,000
└── Tax: ₲4,000,000/year (~$500)
```

### Example 3: Dividends from Dutch company

```
Situation:
├── Dividends from Dutch company: €30,000/year
└ Paraguayan tax resident

Result in Paraguay:
├── Tax: €0 (foreign source)
└── Available: €30,000 (not taxed in PY)
```

## 5. Tax Residence

### Tax Residence Criteria

| Criterion | Definition |
|:----------|:-----------|
| Habitual abode | Main home location |
| Center of vital interests | Family, business, social ties |
| 183-day rule | Physical presence |

### Residency vs Immigration

| Immigration Status | Tax Implication |
|:-------------------|:---------------|
| Tourist | Non-resident — only PY income taxed |
| Temporary | Resident — worldwide income (territorial exemption) |
| Permanent | Resident — worldwide income (territorial exemption) |

:::{.callout-warning}
**Important:** Paraguay participates in CRS (Common Reporting Standard) since 2017. Bank accounts are reported to your country of residence.
:::

## 8. Frequently Asked Questions

### How much tax do I pay if I work remotely for a European client?

**Zero.** If the client is outside Paraguay and services are rendered outside, the income is foreign source → 0% in Paraguay.

### Do I need to declare accounts in Paraguay in my home country?

**Yes.** Paraguay participates in CRS. You must declare the account in your home country tax return.

### Can I avoid IRP if I'm not a tax resident?

If you're a tourist (<183 days) and without residency, you only tax on Paraguayan-sourced income.

### Does the Spain treaty eliminate double taxation?

**Partially.** The treaty reduces dividend withholding, but doesn't eliminate taxation in the source country.
